examples.en: Please listen carefully to what the teacher says.
I always took my parents' advice to heart.

examples.ko: 친구가 해 준 이야기를 새겨들을 필요가 있어요.
examples.en: You need to listen carefully to what your friend told you.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 남의 말을 새겨듣지 않아요.
examples.en: That person doesn't really listen to what others say.

examples.ko: 이번 안내 방송은 꼭 새겨들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please be sure to listen carefully to this announcement.

examples.ko: 비판도 새겨들으면 약이 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you take criticism to heart, it can do you good.

explain: '듣다'보다 말의 뜻을 마음에 담아 두려는 느낌이 강해요. 충고, 가르침, 주의 사항처럼 중요한 말에 쓰고, '귀담아듣다'와 비슷하게 써요. ㄷ불규칙이라서 '새겨들어요', '새겨들으면'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '듣다' because you try to keep the meaning in your mind. Use it for important words such as advice, lessons and warnings; it is close to '귀담아듣다'. It is a ㄷ-irregular verb, so it becomes '새겨들어요' and '새겨들으면'.

examples.en: The baby is sleeping peacefully in the cradle.
My younger sibling fell asleep softly beside me.
I could hear soft, even breathing, so I didn't wake them.

examples.ko: 아이들이 새근새근 자는 모습을 보면 마음이 편해요.
examples.en: Watching the children sleep softly puts my mind at ease.
The puppy also sleeps softly with its belly showing.

examples.ko: 새근새근 잠든 아기 얼굴이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The face of the baby sleeping softly is so pretty.

explain: 아기나 어린아이가 고르고 조용하게 숨 쉬며 자는 모습에 써요. 주로 '자다', '잠들다'와 같이 나와요. 소리가 작고 평온한 느낌이라 시끄럽게 코를 고는 잠에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: It describes a baby or small child sleeping with calm, even breaths. It usually appears with '자다' or '잠들다'. The feeling is quiet and peaceful, so it doesn't fit loud snoring.

examples.ko: 그 노래를 들으니 옛 기억이 새록새록 떠올라요.
examples.en: Hearing that song brings old memories back one after another.

examples.ko: 오랜만에 고향에 오니 추억이 새록새록 생각나요.
examples.en: Coming back to my hometown after a long time, memories come back to me.

examples.ko: 아이 사진을 보면 그때 일이 새록새록 떠올라요.
examples.en: When I look at photos of my child, I recall that time vividly.

examples.ko: 졸업 앨범을 펼치자 친구들 얼굴이 새록새록 기억나요.
examples.en: When I opened the yearbook, my friends' faces came back to me one by one.

examples.ko: 시간이 지나도 그날의 감동이 새록새록 느껴져요.
examples.en: Even as time passes, I keep feeling the emotion of that day anew.

examples.ko: 낡은 편지를 읽으니 그리움이 새록새록 살아나요.
examples.en: Reading the old letter makes my longing come alive again.

explain: '떠오르다', '생각나다', '기억나다'처럼 기억과 감정을 말하는 동사와 같이 써요. 한 번에 확 생각나는 게 아니라 하나씩 새롭게 자꾸 되살아나는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It goes with verbs of memory and feeling such as '떠오르다', '생각나다' and '기억나다'. It is not a sudden flash of memory but the feeling that things keep coming back fresh, one by one.

examples.en: Around dawn today the rain suddenly stopped.
When dawn came, the weather turned chilly.
We reached the mountain top around daybreak.

examples.ko: 새벽녘까지 시험 공부를 하느라 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I studied for the exam until dawn and couldn't sleep.
The streets at daybreak are quiet and clear.
I woke up around dawn and opened the window.

explain: '새벽'은 시간대 전체를 말하고, '새벽녘'은 날이 밝아 올 무렵을 가리켜요. '새벽녘에'처럼 때를 나타낼 때 많이 써요. 비슷한 모양의 '해 질 녘'은 해가 질 무렵이에요.
explain_en: '새벽' covers the whole early-morning period, while '새벽녘' points to the time when day is about to break. It is used in the form '새벽녘에' to say when something happened. The similar '해 질 녘' means around sunset.

examples.en: The apples ripened bright red in the autumn sun.
I was so embarrassed that my face turned bright red.

examples.ko: 새빨간 장미 한 송이를 선물로 받았어요.
examples.en: I received a single deep red rose as a gift.
My nose is bright red from the cold weather.
The sunset dyed the sky bright red.
I cried all night, so my eyes are swollen and bright red.

explain: '빨갛다' 앞에 '새-'가 붙어서 아주 짙고 선명한 빨강을 말해요. ㅎ불규칙이라서 '새빨개요', '새빨간', '새빨갛게'로 바뀌어요. 같은 계열의 '시뻘겋다'는 더 크고 거센 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 그 사람 말은 모두 새빨간 거짓말이었어요.
phrases.en: Everything that person said was a total lie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금도 사실이 아닌 뻔한 거짓말을 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to stress a lie that has no truth in it at all.

explain_en: Adding '새-' to '빨갛다' gives a very deep, vivid red. It is a ㅎ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '새빨개요', '새빨간' and '새빨갛게'. The related '시뻘겋다' feels bigger and heavier.

examples.en: I slept curled up on the bus, so my neck hurts.

examples.ko: 좁은 방이라 새우잠을 잘 수밖에 없었어요.
examples.en: The room was small, so I had no choice but to sleep curled up.
My whole body aches from sleeping curled up last night.
I slept curled up on the sofa and now my back hurts.
It's hard to even sleep curled up on this chair.
I spent the night in a cramped sleep on a hospital chair.

explain: 몸을 새우처럼 웅크리고 불편하게 자는 잠을 말해서, 보통 '새우잠을 자다'로 써요. 짧게 조금 자는 '쪽잠'과는 달리 자는 자세에 초점이 있어요.
explain_en: It means sleeping curled up like a shrimp in an uncomfortable position, usually as '새우잠을 자다'. Unlike '쪽잠' (a short snatch of sleep), the focus is on the sleeping posture.

examples.en: When I was little, I made a slingshot and played with it.

examples.ko: 아이가 새총으로 종이 공을 쏘고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is shooting paper balls with a slingshot.

examples.ko: 새총 고무줄이 끊어져서 더 못 써요.
examples.en: The slingshot's rubber band snapped, so I can't use it anymore.
In the countryside, kids make slingshots out of branches.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 새총 만드는 법을 가르쳐 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather taught me how to make a slingshot.
It's dangerous to shoot a slingshot toward people.

explain: Y자 모양 나뭇가지나 막대에 고무줄을 묶어 돌멩이 같은 것을 날리는 도구예요. 이름에 '총'이 있지만 고무줄의 힘으로 쏘고, 어린 시절 놀이 이야기에서 많이 만나요. '물총'과는 다른 물건이에요.
explain_en: It is a tool made from a Y-shaped branch or stick and a rubber band that flings small things such as stones. Although the name has '총' (gun), it works by the pull of the band, and you meet it in stories about childhood play. It is a different thing from a '물총' (water gun).

examples.ko: 아버지는 마흔 살부터 새치가 나기 시작했어요.
examples.en: My father started getting gray hairs from the age of forty.
I found a gray hair while looking in the mirror.

examples.ko: 새치 때문에 염색을 해야 하나 고민돼요.
examples.en: I'm wondering whether to dye my hair because of the gray hairs.

examples.ko: 요즘 새치가 부쩍 늘어서 신경 쓰여요.
examples.en: My gray hairs have increased a lot lately and it bothers me.

examples.ko: 머리를 빗다가 새치 몇 가닥을 뽑았어요.
examples.en: While combing my hair, I pulled out a few gray strands.
I'm young but have a lot of gray hair, which worries me.

explain: 나이가 많지 않은데 검은 머리 사이에 섞여 나는 흰 머리카락이에요. 일상에서는 그냥 '흰머리'라고도 하고, '새치가 나다', '새치가 생기다'로 써요. '새치기'와 소리가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It means white hairs mixed into dark hair when a person is not that old. In daily talk people also just say '흰머리', and it is used as '새치가 나다' or '새치가 생기다'. It sounds like '새치기' but is a completely different word.

en: cutting in line; line jumping; line jumper

examples.ko: 줄을 서지 않고 새치기하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not cut in line without waiting your turn.
The person ahead cut in line, so I got angry.
I feel bad when I see someone cutting in line.
Even if you're in a hurry, please don't cut in line.

examples.ko: 버스를 탈 때 새치기한 사람이 있었어요.
examples.en: There was someone who cut in line when boarding the bus.
Line-cutting was so bad that a staff member made an announcement.

explain: '새치기하다'로도, '새치기를 하다'로도 써요. 줄을 선 곳에서 차례를 어기고 끼어드는 것을 말하고, 운전할 때는 보통 '끼어들기'라고 해요. '새치'(흰머리)와 소리가 비슷하지만 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It can be used as '새치기하다' or '새치기를 하다'. It refers to breaking the order where people are lined up, and while driving people usually say '끼어들기'. It sounds like '새치' (gray hair) but is a different word.

examples.en: I was so shocked that my face turned pale.

examples.ko: 추운 데서 오래 있었더니 입술이 새파래졌어요.
examples.en: I stayed in the cold for a long time, and my lips turned blue.
The sky is clear, so the sea looks an even deeper blue.
When people get scared, their faces can go pale.

examples.ko: 그는 나쁜 소식을 듣고 새파래진 얼굴로 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat there with a pale face after hearing the bad news.

examples.ko: 아이가 물놀이를 오래 해서 새파래져서 나왔어요.
examples.en: The child swam for so long that he came out turned blue.

explain: '새파랗다'에 '-아지다'가 붙은 말로, 놀람, 추위, 두려움 때문에 얼굴이나 입술 색이 파랗게 변할 때 써요. 같은 상황에서 '얼굴이 파랗게 질리다'라고도 해요. 바다나 하늘의 짙은 파란색 변화에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It comes from '새파랗다' plus '-아지다' and is used when someone's face or lips turn blue because of shock, cold or fear. In the same situation people also say '얼굴이 파랗게 질리다'. It can also describe the sea or sky turning a deeper blue.

examples.en: On New Year's Day the children wore pretty saekdong clothes.

examples.ko: 색동옷은 여러 색의 천을 이어서 만들어요.
examples.en: Saekdong clothes are made by joining cloth of many colors.
The grandmother gave her granddaughter a saekdong outfit.

examples.ko: 색동옷 입은 아이들이 한복 공연을 했어요.
examples.en: Children in saekdong clothes put on a hanbok performance.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 색동옷 체험 행사를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The museum is holding an event to try on saekdong clothes.
The colorful stripes of the saekdong clothes are really pretty.

explain: 여러 가지 색의 줄무늬 천을 이어 소매 등에 단 한복으로, 주로 아이들이 명절에 입는 옷을 떠올려요. 명절에 새로 입는 옷은 '설빔'이라고 하는데 색동옷이 그 대표적인 예예요. 색동저고리라고도 불러요.
explain_en: It is hanbok with stripes of many colors joined together, for example on the sleeves, and you usually picture children wearing it on holidays. New clothes worn for the holiday are called '설빔', and saekdong clothes are a typical example. It is also called '색동저고리'.

examples.en: The sunlight was strong, so I put on tinted glasses.
It's hard to walk along the beach without tinted glasses.

examples.ko: 이 색안경이 얼굴에 정말 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: These tinted glasses really suit your face.
I left my tinted glasses in the car when I got out.
The glare was bright, so I wore tinted glasses while driving.

examples.ko: 가게에서 마음에 드는 색안경을 하나 골랐어요.
examples.en: I picked out a pair of tinted glasses I liked at the store.

explain: 눈을 보호하려고 쓰는 짙은 색 안경이에요. 일상에서는 '선글라스'라고도 하는데, '색안경'은 편견을 가진 시선을 말할 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Don't look at someone with prejudice just because they're a foreigner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선입견이나 편견을 가지고 어떤 사람이나 일을 바라본다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means looking at a person or matter with preconceptions or bias.
phrases.en_equiv: view through tinted glasses; look with a biased eye

explain_en: It is dark-tinted glasses worn to protect the eyes. In daily talk people also say '선글라스', but '색안경' is the word often used for a prejudiced way of looking at someone.

examples.en: The children made paper flowers out of colored paper.

examples.ko: 선생님이 색지를 한 장씩 나눠 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher handed out a sheet of colored paper to each of us.

examples.ko: 빨간 색지가 다 떨어져서 문구점에 가야 해요.
examples.en: We ran out of red colored paper, so I have to go to the stationery store.

examples.ko: 파란 색지에 편지를 써서 친구에게 줬어요.
examples.en: I wrote a letter on blue paper and gave it to my friend.

examples.ko: 색지 한 묶음을 사서 교실 게시판을 꾸몄어요.
examples.en: I bought a bundle of colored paper and decorated the classroom board.
This colored paper is thin, so it's easy to fold.

explain: 색깔이 있는 종이를 말해요. '색종이'는 접거나 오리기 쉽게 작게 자른 종이를 떠올리게 하는 반면, '색지'는 꾸미기나 만들기에 쓰는 종이를 넓게 가리킬 수 있어요.
explain_en: It means paper that has a color. '색종이' brings to mind small paper cut for folding or cutting out, whereas '색지' can refer more broadly to paper used for decorating and crafts.

examples.en: The main road was blocked, so we went around by a side road.
Walking along the path through the forest is refreshing.

examples.ko: 지름길인 줄 알았는데 샛길이 막혀 있었어요.
examples.en: I thought it was a shortcut, but the side road was blocked.
Cars can't enter this side road.
The child was playing on a side path and got lost.

examples.ko: 논 사이의 샛길을 지나 건널목에 이르렀어요.
examples.en: We passed along a path between the rice fields and reached the crossing.

explain: 큰길에서 갈라져 나온 작은 길이에요. 빠르게 가는 '지름길'과는 달리, 단지 크기가 작은 길이라 돌아가거나 한적한 곳을 걸을 때 써요. 이야기나 행동이 본래 방향에서 벗어날 때 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: The story went off on a tangent and I forgot the main point.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 행동이 중심에서 벗어나 다른 쪽으로 흘러간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means that speech or behavior drifts away from the main point.

explain_en: It is a small path that branches off from a main road. Unlike '지름길' (a shortcut that is faster), it simply means a small road, so it is used for detours or quiet walks. It is also used figuratively when a story or action drifts away from the main direction.

examples.ko: 월세와 식비만 따져도 최저 생계비가 꽤 많이 들어요.
examples.en: Even counting only rent and food, the minimum cost of living is quite high.
I work part-time to earn tuition and living expenses.
Prices went up, so the burden of living costs has grown.

examples.ko: 복지 정책에서는 최저 생계비를 어떻게 정할지가 늘 쟁점이 돼요.
examples.en: In welfare policy, how to set the minimum living cost is always an issue.

examples.ko: 이 월급으로는 한 달 생계비도 모자라요.
examples.en: This salary isn't even enough for a month's living expenses.

examples.ko: 유학 생활에서는 학비보다 생계비가 더 부담돼요.
examples.en: When studying abroad, living expenses are more of a burden than tuition.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '생활비'를 더 많이 말하고, '생계비'는 먹고사는 데 꼭 필요한 돈이라는 느낌이 있어서 복지, 뉴스, 정책 이야기에 자주 나와요. 특히 '최저 생계비'처럼 기준이 되는 금액을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: In everyday talk people say '생활비' more, while '생계비' carries the sense of money you need just to make a living, so it shows up in talk about welfare, news and policy. It is used especially for a standard amount, as in '최저 생계비'.

examples.en: Please keep raw meat in the refrigerator.
I bought fresh raw meat at the market.

examples.ko: 생고기를 만진 손은 꼭 씻어야 해요.
examples.en: You must wash your hands after touching raw meat.

examples.ko: 생고기와 채소는 도마를 따로 쓰는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to use separate cutting boards for raw meat and vegetables.
This restaurant brings in its raw meat on the same day.

examples.ko: 생고기에서 이상한 냄새가 나면 먹지 마세요.
examples.en: If the raw meat smells strange, don't eat it.

explain: 익히지 않은 고기를 말하고 '날고기'와 비슷하게 써요. 요리 전에 손질하거나 보관하는 상황에서 자주 나와요. 익힌 고기는 '구운 고기', '삶은 고기'처럼 방법을 붙여서 말해요.
explain_en: It means meat that has not been cooked and is used much like '날고기'. It comes up when preparing or storing meat before cooking. Cooked meat is described with the method, such as '구운 고기' or '삶은 고기'.

examples.en: I took a wrong turn and went through needless hardship.

examples.ko: 괜한 생고생 하지 말고 택시를 타세요.
examples.en: Don't go through pointless trouble; just take a taxi.
I left without preparing and only suffered for nothing.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 생고생해서 감기에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I had a miserable time in the rain and caught a cold.
Because of one mistake, everyone is going through needless hardship.

examples.ko: 그렇게 생고생을 하고도 상을 못 받았어요.
examples.en: After all that trouble, I still didn't win a prize.

explain: 안 해도 될 고생이나 괜히 하는 고생을 말해요. 불평하거나 아쉬울 때 하는 구어체 느낌이 강해요. '생고생하다', '생고생을 하다' 둘 다 쓰고, 보람 없는 고생은 '헛고생'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It means hardship you didn't have to go through, or effort that was in vain. It has a strongly colloquial feel and is used when complaining or feeling regret. Both '생고생하다' and '생고생을 하다' are used, and fruitless effort is also called '헛고생'.

examples.en: Since it's in season, raw oysters are really tasty in winter.
I ate raw oysters and got an upset stomach.
I dip raw oysters in vinegared red pepper paste.
Fresh raw oysters smell of the sea.

examples.ko: 저는 생굴은 못 먹고 익힌 굴만 먹어요.
examples.en: I can't eat raw oysters, only cooked ones.
I bought a bag of raw oysters at the market.

explain: 익히지 않은 굴을 말해요. '굴'이라고만 해도 되지만 익힌 굴과 구별하고 싶을 때 '생굴'이라고 해요. 익힌 굴 요리로는 '굴전', '굴국밥' 등이 있어요.
explain_en: It means oysters that have not been cooked. You can just say '굴', but '생굴' is used when you want to tell them apart from cooked oysters. Cooked oyster dishes include '굴전' and '굴국밥'.

examples.en: The baby looks at me and smiles sweetly.
The clerk greeted me with a bright smile, which made me feel good.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 언제 봐도 생글생글 밝아요.
examples.en: That child always looks cheerful and smiling whenever I see her.
My daughter ran to the front door with a smile.
That smiling face is so cute.

examples.ko: 무슨 좋은 일이 있는지 하루 종일 생글생글 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: She's been smiling all day, as if something good happened.

explain: 소리 없이 눈과 입으로 부드럽게 자꾸 웃는 모습이에요. '웃다', '인사하다'와 자주 같이 쓰고, 한 번 웃는 '생긋'과 달리 계속 웃는 느낌이에요. 비슷한 말로 '방긋방긋'도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes smiling softly and repeatedly with the eyes and mouth, without sound. It goes with '웃다' or '인사하다', and unlike '생긋', which is a single smile, it feels continuous. A similar word is '방긋방긋'.

examples.en: The child smiled and waved a hand.
She smiled and greeted me when she saw me.
When I took the photo, my younger sibling gave a little smile.

examples.ko: 수줍은 듯 생긋 웃고 대답하지 않았어요.
examples.en: She gave a shy smile and didn't answer.
The teacher smiled gently and praised me.
When the baby smiled, everyone was delighted.

explain: 눈과 입으로 소리 없이 가볍게 한 번 웃는 모습이에요. 계속 웃는 '생글생글'과 달리 한 번의 웃음에 써요. 주로 '웃다', '인사하다' 앞에 와요.
explain_en: It describes a light, silent smile with the eyes and mouth, once. Unlike '생글생글', which is a continuing smile, it is used for a single smile. It mostly comes before '웃다' or '인사하다'.

examples.en: Raw material prices rose, so production costs went up.
The company moved its factory to cut production costs.
Production costs include material costs and labor costs.
The product price went up because of production costs.

examples.ko: 농가는 비료값이 올라 생산비 부담이 커졌어요.
examples.en: Fertilizer prices rose, so farms face a heavier production cost burden.

examples.ko: 생산비를 낮추면 더 싸게 팔 수 있어요.
examples.en: If production costs go down, we can sell at a lower price.

explain: 물건을 만드는 데 드는 돈을 말해요. 팔 때 받는 값이 아니라 만들 때 쓴 돈이고, 보통 '생산비가 들다', '생산비가 늘다', '생산비를 줄이다'로 써요. 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 가격이 오른 이유를 설명할 때 나와요.
explain_en: It means the money spent on making goods. It is what was spent in making, not the price you get when selling, and it is used as '생산비가 들다', '생산비가 늘다' or '생산비를 줄이다'. It appears in news and economic talk when explaining why prices rose.

examples.en: This year's semiconductor production value rose sharply.
Production value statistics are announced in the news every month.

examples.ko: 이 공장의 연간 생산액은 천억 원이에요.
examples.en: This factory's annual production value is 100 billion won.

examples.ko: 생산액이 줄면 일자리도 줄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If production value drops, jobs can drop too.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 자동차 생산액을 비교해 보세요.
examples.en: Compare the two countries' car production values.

examples.ko: 우리 지역 생산액이 전국에서 가장 높아요.
examples.en: Our region's production value is the highest in the country.

explain: 만들어 낸 물건의 양이 아니라 그 값을 돈으로 계산한 금액이에요. 개수나 양을 말할 때는 '생산량'을 써서 구별해요. 경제 뉴스나 통계에서 자주 만나요.
explain_en: It is the money value of what was produced, not the quantity. To talk about number or volume you use '생산량', so the two are kept apart. You will meet it often in economic news and statistics.

examples.ko: 기자는 불이 난 현장에서 생중계를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The reporter is broadcasting live from the scene of the fire.

examples.ko: 월드컵 경기를 생중계로 보려고 일찍 일어났어요.
examples.en: I got up early to watch the World Cup match live.

examples.ko: 오늘 밤 시상식은 생중계를 하지 않는대요.
examples.en: I heard they won't broadcast tonight's award ceremony live.
The sound suddenly cut out during the live broadcast.
I started a live stream on my phone for the fans.

examples.ko: 생중계는 실수해도 다시 할 수 없어서 긴장돼요.
examples.en: With live coverage you can't redo mistakes, so I get nervous.

explain: '생방송'은 방송 프로그램이 지금 나가는 것을 말하고, '생중계'는 경기나 행사나 사건의 현장을 그 자리에서 바로 보여 주는 것을 말해요. 보통 '생중계를 하다', '생중계로 보다'로 써요.
explain_en: '생방송' means a program going out live, while '생중계' means showing a game, event or incident right as it happens on the spot. It is usually used as '생중계를 하다' or '생중계로 보다'.

examples.ko: 기자는 불이 난 현장의 상황을 생중계하고 있어요.
examples.en: The reporter is broadcasting the situation at the fire scene live.
The broadcaster airs the final live from start to finish.
Today's opening ceremony was also broadcast live online.
The mayor decided to broadcast the meeting live.
They will broadcast the concert live on this channel.

examples.ko: 현장을 생중계하면 많은 사람이 바로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you broadcast the scene live, many people can watch right away.

explain: '경기를 생중계하다', '행사를 생중계하다'처럼 현장에서 일어나는 일을 그 자리에서 바로 보여 준다는 느낌으로 써요. '생중계를 하다'로 나누어 말해도 같은 뜻이에요. 방송국, 기자, 개인 채널 모두 주어가 될 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is used for showing what is happening on the spot right away, as in '경기를 생중계하다' or '행사를 생중계하다'. You can split it as '생중계를 하다' with the same meaning. The subject can be a broadcaster, a reporter or a personal channel.

examples.en: Yesterday we decorated the wedding hall beautifully with fresh flowers.
I bought real flowers, not artificial ones.
Real flowers wilt quickly after a few days.
The scent of real flowers fills the room.

examples.ko: 이 꽃집은 조화 없이 생화만 팔아요.
examples.en: This flower shop sells only real flowers, no artificial ones.
There are many artificial flowers that look like real ones.

explain: 살아 있는 식물에서 딴 진짜 꽃을 말하고, 종이나 천으로 만든 '조화'와 짝을 이뤄요. 평소에는 그냥 '꽃'이라고 하다가 조화와 구별할 때 '생화'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means a real flower cut from a living plant, and it pairs with '조화', flowers made of paper or cloth. Usually people just say '꽃', and use '생화' when they want to tell it apart from artificial flowers.

examples.en: Because of the drought, household water has run short.
This dam supplies household water to the city.

examples.ko: 생활용수를 아끼려면 양치할 때 물을 잠가요.
examples.en: To save household water, turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.

examples.ko: 마을에는 생활용수로 쓸 우물이 하나 있어요.
examples.en: The village has one well to use for household water.
Household water use goes up in summer.
The water supply was cut off for a while because of the typhoon.

explain: 집이나 일상생활에서 마시고 씻고 요리하는 데 쓰는 물이에요. 농사에 쓰는 '농업용수', 공장에서 쓰는 '공업용수'와 구별해서 말해요. 가뭄이나 물 절약 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is the water used at home and in daily life for drinking, washing and cooking. It is set apart from '농업용수' (farming water) and '공업용수' (industrial water). It often appears in news about drought and saving water.

examples.en: The volunteer group quickly supplied daily necessities to the flood victims.
When you move, you have to buy the daily necessities first.
Toilet paper and soap are typical daily necessities.
Prices rose, so the cost of daily necessities is a burden.

examples.ko: 이 마트에서는 생활필수품을 한꺼번에 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this mart you can buy daily necessities all at once.

examples.ko: 비상 가방에 생활필수품 몇 가지를 챙겨 두세요.
examples.en: Keep a few daily necessities packed in your emergency bag.

explain: 살아가는 데 꼭 있어야 하는 물건을 말하고, 줄여서 '생필품'이라고도 해요. 재난 지원, 이사, 물가 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 꼭 필요하지 않은 '사치품'과 대비돼요.
explain_en: It means goods you must have to live, and it is often shortened to '생필품'. It appears in talk about disaster relief, moving and prices. It contrasts with '사치품' (luxury goods) that are not essential.

examples.ko: 호텔 로비에 큰 샹들리에가 걸려 있어요.
examples.en: A large chandelier hangs in the hotel lobby.

examples.ko: 밤이 되자 샹들리에 불빛이 반짝반짝 빛나요.
examples.en: When night falls, the chandelier lights sparkle.
You need a ladder to clean the chandelier.
We took a photo under the big chandelier.

examples.ko: 우리 집 거실에 작은 샹들리에를 달았어요.
examples.en: We hung a small chandelier in our living room.
This chandelier is made from pieces of glass.

explain: 프랑스어에서 온 외래어로, 여러 개의 전구나 유리 장식이 달린 화려한 천장 조명을 말해요. 평범한 천장 등은 '전등'이나 '조명'이라고 해서 구별해요. 호텔, 극장, 결혼식장 같은 곳에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: This loanword from French refers to a fancy ceiling light with many bulbs or glass decorations. Ordinary ceiling lights are called '전등' or '조명', so the two are kept apart. You often see chandeliers in hotels, theaters and wedding halls.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 서구적 시각에서 벗어났다는 점이 특별해요.
examples.en: That movie is special because it breaks away from a Western viewpoint.
He has a Western way of thinking.
This building has a strongly Western feel.

examples.ko: 서구적 가치만으로 세상을 보면 놓치는 것이 많아요.
examples.en: If you see the world only through Western values, you miss a lot.
That singer is famous for Western-looking features.
Our home's interior has a Western atmosphere.

explain: 유럽이나 서양의 문화, 생각, 모습을 닮았다는 뜻으로 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며요. 반대되는 말은 '동양적'이에요. '서구적인 분위기', '서구적으로'처럼 '-적이다' 형태로도 써요.
explain_en: It modifies the noun that follows and means resembling the culture, ideas or look of Europe or the West. The opposite is '동양적'. It can also take the '-적이다' form, as in '서구적인 분위기' and '서구적으로'.

examples.ko: 식생활의 서구화로 빵을 먹는 사람이 늘었어요.
examples.en: With the westernization of eating habits, more people eat bread.

examples.ko: 서구화가 빨라지면서 전통 문화가 줄어든다고 걱정하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people worry that traditional culture is shrinking as westernization speeds up.

examples.ko: 한복 대신 양복을 입는 것도 서구화의 한 모습이에요.
examples.en: Wearing suits instead of hanbok is also one form of westernization.

examples.ko: 도시의 서구화는 건물 모양에서도 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Westernization in cities can also be seen in the shape of buildings.
Views on westernization differ from generation to generation.
There are also voices worried about excessive westernization.

explain: 생활, 문화, 제도가 서양식으로 바뀌는 과정을 말해요. '서구화되다', '서구화하다'로 쓸 수 있고, 단순히 새로워지는 '현대화'와는 서양을 닮아 간다는 점에서 달라요. 주로 사회나 문화를 설명하는 글에서 만나요.
explain_en: It refers to the process by which life, culture or systems change to Western style. It can be used as '서구화되다' or '서구화하다', and differs from '현대화' (modernization) in that it means becoming like the West. You mostly meet it in writing that explains society or culture.
